clue.text: May's former position as the country's leader

definitions.meaning: Peter May, the cricketer, once led the national side, so this is the job he held
the person who leads the nation's team on the field

explanation.surface: A remark about Theresa May having once been prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Theresa May; the clue means Peter May, who captained England at cricket in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name the captaincy of the national team: one historical holder, and the general idea of its skipper.

clue.text: Bush, say (American chap) — and now Cameron?

parts.note: the elder is a shrub, an example of a bush
playfully, a man of the States is a States-man

explanation.surface: A comparison of a former US president with David Cameron in retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like the president, but it is a plant; 'American chap' is split as a man of the States.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired senior politician such as Cameron, after leaving office, is described as a respected veteran of public life.

clue.text: On fast track up, Osborne finally failed the country

indicators.note: the last letter of the first name fails to appear, so it is dropped

parts.note: George Osborne, the former Chancellor

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the road name is read bottom to top

parts.note: the A1 is a major fast road in Britain

explanation.surface: A politician on a fast track to promotion who let the country down.
explanation.walkthrough: GEORGE loses its final E to give GEORG; A1, read with I for 1 and turned by 'up', gives IA, placed on GEORG. The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgia is a nation in the Caucasus, so it is an instance of a country.

clue.text: 15 seconds to get simple cocktail dress on?

definitions.note: a rugby union side has fifteen players; this is New Zealand's national team

parts.note: an all-black frock, the little black number, is the classic plain cocktail dress

explanation.surface: Getting into a little black dress in moments before a party.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' stands alone as the definition: New Zealand's rugby union side fields fifteen players. 'to get ... on' puts S after the dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Zealand national rugby union side, fifteen strong, is nicknamed for its black kit.

clue.text: Prevented plot arising: fought, while heading off

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for plot reads upwards

parts.note: a flower bed is a garden plot

indicators.note: the first letter, its head, is taken off

parts.note: warred means fought

explanation.surface: A conspiracy stopped before it got going, after a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns BED into DEB; 'heading off' strips W from WARRED, leaving ARRED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be barred from something is to be stopped or kept out, a synonym of prevented.

clue.text: Impressive eventual successor to May

definitions.meaning: the month that follows May, after June

explanation.surface: Speculation about whoever will eventually take over from Theresa May.
explanation.walkthrough: The successor is not a politician but a month, coming two after May.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means grand or dignified; the noun is the calendar month two after May.

clue.text: Athenian turmoil is May's opportunity — new leaders wanted

indicators.note: only the leading letter of each of these five words is wanted

explanation.surface: Political chaos as a chance for the prime minister to bring in new leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: Timon of Athens is the title character of Shakespeare's play about a misanthrope.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Timon is a citizen of Athens, so he is an example of an Athenian.

clue.text: High-status woman elected, taking fizzy drink

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in
Fanta is a brand of orange soda

explanation.surface: A prominent woman wins an election and celebrates with a soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An infanta is a daughter of a Spanish or Portuguese monarch, so a woman of royal rank.

clue.text: Failing opportunity, turn up to get university position

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing
a chance is an opportunity

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word for turn is read upwards

parts.note: a roll is a turn, as in a rolling over

explanation.surface: Someone who misses a chance then turns up to claim an academic post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ROLL into LLOR at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities this title names the chief executive officer, the head of the institution in practice.

clue.text: Scribble leads to error in flyer — that's dangerous

parts.note: a doodle is an idle scribble
a bug is an error, as in software

explanation.surface: A careless scribble causing an error on an aircraft that is then unsafe.
explanation.walkthrough: The doodlebug was the wartime nickname for the German V-1 flying bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: The V-1 flying bomb was an unpiloted explosive aircraft, so a perilous thing that flew.

clue.text: A figure of authority in plain clothes

definitions.meaning: a Muslim scholar empowered to issue legal rulings
civilian dress worn by someone normally in uniform

explanation.surface: An official going about undercover in ordinary dress.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an Islamic jurist; the other is civilian clothing, as in being out of uniform.

clue.text: One of the stars in the state, begin to work

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
plans that gel start to come together and work

explanation.surface: A celebrity in a state starting to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigel is the brightest star in the constellation Orion, an example of a star.

clue.text: Nag raved endlessly: nothing wrong in that

indicators.note: the two short pieces are placed within the shortened word
the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: ranted means raved
O is the figure zero, nothing
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: Someone who nagged and raved, insisting there was nothing wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a verb but is a noun: Rosinante is Don Quixote's horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Quixote's broken-down horse is the most famous literary example of an old nag.

clue.text: May's predecessor, the well-known revolutionary meeting resistance

parts.note: 'that' points to someone famous, as in 'that Mr Smith'
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An earlier prime minister described as a famous radical facing opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher was the female prime minister before Theresa May, preceding her as a woman in the role.

clue.text: In window frame place prominent slogan

indicators.note: the abbreviation for place goes inside the frame

parts.note: a sash is the frame holding a window's glass
PL is the abbreviation for place in street names

explanation.surface: Putting a big slogan in the frame of a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is a prominent headline or eye-catching display in a newspaper.

clue.text: Southern Region has a name for plunging in dagger? No way

indicators.note: the two pieces are thrust into the shortened word, like a blade
RD, the abbreviation for road, a way, is removed

parts.note: a poniard is a slim dagger
a tag is a name or label

explanation.surface: A region with a name for its daggers, which nobody wants plunged in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No way' leaves PONIA, which the A and TAG pieces are plunged into after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Patagonia is the region at the southern tip of South America.

clue.text: Veto our side employing a bitch, regularly vulgar

parts.note: to ban is to veto
us means our side

indicators.note: every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A ban on a dog being employed by our team, routinely crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of 'bitch', I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Banausic means merely mechanical or utilitarian and so lacking refinement.

clue.text: May's not hard: a saint?

indicators.note: the letter for hard is not included

parts.note: Theresa is May's first name
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A query whether Mrs May is soft and saintly.
explanation.definitionFit: St Teresa of Avila is the best known saint with the name.

clue.text: Put in new position in unexpected delight

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit inside the word for unexpected

parts.note: something rare is uncommon and so unexpected

indicators.note: the letters of the word put are placed in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Being moved to a new job brings unexpected joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in new position' turns PUT into PTU, which goes 'in' RARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapture is a state of intense joy, a stronger synonym for delight.

clue.text: What's wrong with a sort of "Right Hon" for May?

indicators.note: the letters are put wrong, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking what is amiss with calling the prime minister a Right Honourable.
explanation.walkthrough: May here is not the politician but the blossom: 'Right Hon' is the honorific of a Privy Counsellor.
explanation.definitionFit: The hawthorn is commonly called may, after the month it flowers.

clue.text: Working with a parliament, making cuts

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
a diet is a legislative assembly, as in Japan

explanation.surface: A government working with parliament to slash spending.
explanation.walkthrough: The cuts are not to budgets but to what one eats.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restricting food intake is cutting down, so the idiom describes making cuts.

clue.text: What May must do with naval leadership rival?

parts.note: Michael Gove stood against May for the Conservative leadership
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A question about the prime minister's duty given a challenger for the top job.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove, a Conservative minister, ran in the 2016 leadership contest that May won.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime minister's job is to rule the country, so this is her task.

clue.text: Marvellous exact opposite of May, perhaps — a bright star

parts.note: super means marvellous
November lies six months from May, opposite it on the calendar; Nov is its abbreviation

explanation.surface: Praise for someone thought to be the precise reverse of Mrs May, a shining celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: May here is the month: November sits directly across the year from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is an exploding star that briefly becomes extremely luminous.

clue.text: Betray first sign of ruthlessness, a heavyweight

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: Betrayal as the first hint of ruthlessness in a powerful figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat on someone is to inform against them, an idiom for betraying them.

clue.text: Serious start on galvanising party

indicators.note: the starting letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a rave is a lively party

explanation.surface: A solemn beginning to rousing a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and serious are synonyms describing a solemn manner or a weighty matter.

clue.text: Blue and put in lead, ultimately

indicators.note: the letters are placed inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Something sad that was eventually given the leading role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' means not sad but smutty, as in blue films.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes or films are rude ones, and so are adult ones, rated for grown-ups only.

clue.text: Critical of lateness, I blow up

indicators.note: the letters are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at tardiness who loses their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something critical is vital or indispensable, the same as essential.

clue.text: Assuming power, remarkably ardent, can head Westminster team

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take on, or assume, the power symbol inside
the words are arranged in a remarkable new way

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A keen ministerial team in Westminster, taking power under an eager leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Westminster' suggests Parliament but means the Abbey, whose governing body this is.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean and chapter form the governing body of a cathedral or abbey such as Westminster's.
